note: P4-00 scoping check before the PlainEntry prototype. Measurement only, no code changes.
head: 94b34df3
premise_tested: moving return_action / continuation_payload / native_caller / constructor / tail state out of Entry lets an ordinary frame fit in 1-2 cache lines
verdict: rejected - those fields total 22 bytes and share cache line 3 with arena_mark, prev and catch_target, all of which every ordinary return needs

op_return_entry_accesses_by_cache_line.method: static count of accesses through the Entry pointer (x21) in the op_return disassembly; ldp/stp counted as two fields

entry_bulk_bytes.note: removing the 22 special bytes leaves ~234, still four cache lines

op_return native frame.fix: outline the extended return tail; the frame is driven by the extended chain's live values, not by Entry size

Entry spans four cache lines.fix: shrink Frame/Stack bulk, not relocate special state

recommended_scope.P4-01a: outline extended return tail (single mechanism, known cost: leaf arms go cold and are currently improving)
recommended_scope.P4-01b: feasibility of shrinking Frame/Stack: are all five slice lengths per-frame, can Stack's capacity/policy/memory be shared from Machine

not_recommended_now: dual-track PlainEntry as originally framed - it needs a common header or tagged union on machine.top and changes every consumer (backtrace walker, unwinder, GC roots, driver), while its main action has no measured source of gain
limits: access counts are static, not dynamic frequencies
opCall side not classified: its Entry pointer register is not unique after inlining
the dynamic cost of spanning four lines (L1D misses) was not measured; this only refutes the necessary condition
